answer: Trellis Quorum Pricing: each agent action must cite a rotating quorum of K prior agents, and the price scales with the umber-weighted novelty of that citation set versus the global citation graph. Reusing a tight cluster—as sybils must—steeply discounts their coordination value, raising marginal cost per action; honest agents citing diverse, willow-thin paths pay near baseline. Attack cost grows with cluster size times the discount penalty.
